verdict.rationale: BigCommerce's own docs say its REST and GraphQL Management APIs manage products and orders programmatically, with scoped API accounts and a Request Runner for testing. That covers the product-creation and order-editing parts of the story. The evidence never mentions refunds or fulfillment/shipment endpoints, so only about half the lifecycle is documented. missing for 10: documented refund API, documented fulfillment/shipment-triggering API, endpoint-level detail for order editing, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can manage the full commerce lifecycle programmatically — create products, edit orders, issue refunds, trigger fulfillments — through the admin API

citations.quote:
Use REST and GraphQL APIs to manage products, orders,
customers, and store settings programmatically.
You can experiment with our REST Management APIs using the **Request Runner**, which is built in to the [API Reference]
BigCommerce offers three types of OAuth-based API accounts to developers who wish to use BigCommerce's REST APIs: store-level credentials, app-level credentials, and account-level credentials.
